name: Color corrector (peach/orange)

lead: A peach or orange color corrector is a pigmented cosmetic layered under concealer or foundation to cancel blue-purple shadows under the eyes. The brighter, more even under-eye is visible straight away.

It works on color theory: a warm tone opposite blue-purple on the color wheel neutralizes the dark area so it sits closer to the surrounding skin. Wikipedia describes related approaches such as yellow undertones for dark circles and green for redness. Periorbital hyperpigmentation itself is described as an inherited melanin trait.

paras: People dab a small amount onto the darkest part of the under-eye, blend it lightly, then apply concealer or foundation over it. Deeper skin tones tend to use deeper orange shades, lighter tones peach. It lasts for the day and comes off with makeup removal.

The effect is temporary and sits on the skin surface; it does not change the cause of dark circles. No safety data specific to peach correctors were found. As with any cosmetic near the eyes, irritation or allergy to an ingredient is possible.

angle.text: Users layer a peach or orange corrector under concealer to cancel blue-purple under-eye darkness, and the brighter look is visible right away. It is a cosmetic technique that lasts for the day.

lead: A peach or orange color corrector is a cosmetic applied beneath concealer or foundation to neutralize blue-purple tones, most often the discoloration beneath the eyes.

Concealer is a heavily pigmented cosmetic that hides imperfections including dark under-eye circles; Wikipedia describes yellow undertones for dark circles, green and blue to counteract redness, and purple to brighten sallow complexions, and does not mention peach or orange [1]. Max Factor's Erace, launched in 1954, was the first commercially available concealer [1].

Periorbital hyperpigmentation is described as an inherited trait of excess melanin, most prevalent at ages 16 to 25 [2]. No studies on color correctors were found, and the article is thin on sourcing.
infobox: Peach, orange; related yellow, green, purple correctors [1]

paras: Concealers come in liquid, cream, stick, pencil and powder forms and are often used alongside foundation [1]. For dark circles, people usually pick a shade one or two levels lighter than their skin with yellow undertones and set it with powder [1]. Peach and orange correctors extend this layered approach to deeper discoloration, according to makeup users; no source reviewed documents this in detail.

timeline.event: Max Factor's Erace becomes the first commercially available concealer [1].
